gist: Inflation means the same money buys less: US prices roughly doubled since 2000.
The 2021-22 spike had several causes stacked together: money and demand, supply chains, energy and some company pricing.
Inflation quietly moves buying power between shoppers, savers, workers, borrowers and governments.

gist: Tunnels are slow and costly: a standard TBM (tunnel boring machine) digs a mile in 8 to 12 weeks, and big-city lines cost $100 million to $1 billion+ a mile, mostly in stations.

books.title: How Neuralink Works
books.blurb: Juno's lab sketchbook uses one text message as a yardstick: how the brain says "move", Neuralink's implant, robot surgeon and decoder, the real trial speeds, how it compares with the Utah array, Synchron and EEG (brain-wave) caps, where trials and safety stand, and what was promised vs delivered.
gist: Paralysis cuts the path from brain to muscle, but the motor cortex still fires; a BCI (brain-computer interface) reads those spikes and turns them into actions.
Neuralink's N1 puts 1,000+ electrodes on hair-thin threads placed by a robot; the record is 11.32 BPS (bits per second), close to a mouse, and typing reaches 40 words a minute.
Neuralink had 21 people enrolled (Jan 2026) but no approval to sell; safety, animal welfare, price and Musk's timelines are still open questions.

books.title: How Electric Cars Work
books.blurb: Remy's road-trip log uses one 400-mile drive to Grandma's as a yardstick: why EVs (electric vehicles) were stuck, how batteries and motors work, how Tesla's plan and chargers changed the game, what the trip costs vs gas, how the world (and China's BYD) switched, and cameras vs lidar (laser radar) for self-driving.
gist: Around 2010 EVs (electric vehicles) were stuck on short range, costly batteries and slow charging; battery packs are now 93% cheaper.
A battery shuttles lithium ions, a motor chases a spinning magnetic field, and an EV turns 87 to 91% of its energy into motion vs about 30% for gas.
Tesla proved the cars and chargers; now China and BYD lead sales, and the next race is self-driving, Waymo's lidar (laser radar) vs Tesla's cameras.
books.tagline: Lithium on a shuttle, magnets that chase, and one 400-mile road trip.

gist: Humanoids are shaped like us because the world is built for us, but walking, hands and battery life are still hard.
Robots learn in simulation, from human drivers and videos, and from big AI (artificial intelligence) models that split thinking slow from moving fast.
As of Oct 2026 only 13,000 to 18,000 shipped in 2025, mostly from China; real jobs are in factories and warehouses, and homes are still a promise.

books.title: Nuclear for AI
books.blurb: Pip's lab notes follow AI's (artificial intelligence's) electricity hunger back to nuclear power: the 24/7 firm-power problem, how a reactor works, why big plants got slow, small modular reactors' promise vs reality, the fuel and permit gates, big-tech deals, a nuclear vs gas vs solar vs wind comparison, waste and honest risks, as of Oct 2026.
gist: AI (artificial intelligence) data centres need huge amounts of power around the clock, and nuclear runs about 91% of the time with no carbon emissions.
A reactor is a kettle: splitting atoms makes heat, steam spins a turbine, and control rods keep the chain reaction on a leash.
As of Oct 2026 big tech has signed gigawatts of deals, but new small reactors are still years away, so old plants, restarts and gas fill the gap.
books.tagline: Chatbots, chain reactions and a very long waiting line.
